title: Whisper — Architecture & Fine-Tuning
service: LongForm: long-recording transcription around a 30 s Whisper window, with a LoRA budget tool

deviations: Part 1 plans windows in integer samples (plan_windows) and splits the lesson's encoder_frames into mel_frames and encoder_positions, because the lesson's function returns mel frames under an encoder name (quiz Q10c); the off-by-one is the missing 'stop at the end' of chunk_schedule, and the timing bug is a containment scan that hides it.

Part 2 folds build_prompt's validation into to_text and parse and works on the special-token text, not token ids; the domain precision trap is the 0.02 s timestamp grid together with BPE leading spaces.

Part 3 splits each overlap at its midpoint by word timestamps (quiz Q9(c), code exercise 5, the stride logic of chunked pipelines) rather than aligning a longest common run, and adds the short-clip padding pitfall through Part 1's positions.

Part 4 uses consecutive windows with condition_on_previous_text context, as Whisper's own long-form loop does, so it does not depend on Part 3; the repeated-n-gram check drops a looping window and resets the context, and the output is server-sent events rather than the NDJSON used in 06/03.

Part 5 counts LoRA on a module tree of Hugging Face's large-v3-turbo (128 mel bins, vocab 51,866), so the totals come out at the real 808,878,080 base and the lesson's ~3M trainable. Targets match name by name at the end of a module's path, as PEFT's target_modules list does; the shell wildcards per name and the ValueErrors for a target that matches nothing or a non-Linear module are this pack's own rules (PEFT takes a regex string for patterns, raises only when nothing at all matches, and also adapts Embedding and Conv1d layers).
